title: Throughput Assurance: staged degradation staircase, credit algorithm, and autoscale interlocks
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Purpose: define a testable, auditable SLA and error budget model for Dedicated customers that ties into autoscaling controls and a transparent credit calculation. This ticket produces: 1) precise SLO definitions (measurement windows, aggregation, quantiles), 2) a staged degradation matrix for progressive remediation, 3) the SmoothCredit v1 algorithm (proportional credit computation), and 4) contract language snippets for legal/CS/finance review. Scope excludes per-customer legal negotiation templates (handled by sales/legal team).
acceptance_criteria: SLO definition doc with metric names, collection windows, and exact query examples for the Grafana dashboards
A staged degradation matrix with 3 tiers (Degrade-1, Degrade-2, Degrade-3) and automated triggers mapped to autoscaler actions
SmoothCredit v1 formula documented with worked examples and monthly fee integration
Contract clause draft that legal approves for inclusion in Dedicated capacity offer terms
Integration checklist for Eng to emit required metrics (per-customer tokens/min, per-AZ availability, autoscale events)
contract_language_draft: Service Commitment: Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to provide a sustained token throughput of >= CommittedTokensPerMinute (CTPM) measured at the customer account level. Measurement: CTPM is measured as the 5-minute rolling median of per-minute served tokens, aggregated across the customer's dedicated pool and availability zones. Availability Window: all measurements use UTC. Measurement Period and Error Budget: performance is evaluated on a rolling 30-day window. Error budget is defined as the fraction of minutes within the 30-day window where served throughput < 0.9 * CTPM. Credit Trigger: If the error budget exceeds the threshold for the applicable tier (see Degradation Matrix), Customer may be eligible for service credits as described below. Remedies: Redwood will (a) attempt autoscale and burst actions, (b) perform load rebalancing to alternate capacity pools, and (c) notify Customer per the Notice Schedule. Credit Computation: See SmoothCredit v1. Limitations: Credits exclude (i) Customer-triggered throttling, (ii) scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice, and (iii) force majeure events.
smoothcredit_v1_algorithm: Overview: SmoothCredit v1 computes a proportional monthly credit based on observed shortfall magnitude, duration, and customer committed spend. Step 1: For each minute t in the rolling 30-day window compute shortfall s_t = max(0, 1 - (served_t / CTPM)). Step 2: Aggregate shortfall S = sum_t s_t * w_t where w_t is a time-decay weight (default w_t = 1 for all t in the 30-day window; future versions may weight recent incidents higher). Step 3: Normalized shortfall NS = S / (minutes_in_30_day_window). Step 4: Raw credit fraction RCF = clamp(NS, 0, 1). Step 5: Apply tier floor and cap: CreditFraction = max(RCF - TierFloor, 0) * TierMultiplier. Step 6: Monthly credit = CreditFraction * CustomerCommittedMonthlyFee. Worked example: CTPM=120k tokens/min, observed average served at 108k for 10,000 minutes over 30 days -> s_t average 0.1 for those minutes -> S approx 1,000 -> NS = 1000/43200 = 0.023 -> RCF=0.023 -> if TierFloor=0.01 and TierMultiplier=1.5 -> CreditFraction=(0.023-0.01)*1.5=0.0195 -> Monthly credit = 1.95% of committed monthly fee.
staged_degradation_matrix: Degrade-1 (Minor): trigger when shortfall > TierFloor but CreditFraction < 0.05 for rolling 30-day window. Actions: immediate autoscale (if available), 10m convo to customer via email and console banner, engage SE on duty. Autoscale interlock: increase pool by up to 25% instant burst (if pre-warmed capacity exists). Cooldown: 10 minutes. Degrade-2 (Moderate): trigger when CreditFraction between 0.05 and 0.20. Actions: automatic canary reroute to fallback model variant with lower memory footprint, start cross-AZ rebalancing, open incident with SRE and PM. Autoscale interlock: provision reserved burst (60–120m warm-up), queue best-effort requests (non-guaranteed) after guaranteed tokens are served. Degrade-3 (Severe): trigger when CreditFraction >= 0.20 or sustained 90% shortfall for 60 minutes. Actions: failover to secondary region (if configured), offer temporary uplift of reserved capacity (sales-managed), and auto-apply credits per SmoothCredit v1 pending legal review. Customer notification cadence escalates to phone + Slack. Post-incident: automated RCA draft and credit computation report published within 5 business days.
autoscale_policy_spec: Targets: target utilization for dedicated pools set to TokensServedPerGPUUnit with a target of 70%-80% for steady state. Cooldowns: scale-up can occur immediately (subject to pre-warm capacity) but scale-down has a 15-minute cooldown. Burst policy: allow short-term burst up to 40% additional capacity for up to 12 minutes if pre-warmed nodes available; additional bursting requires approval. Admission control: prioritized queues based on 'guaranteed' vs 'best-effort' labels at request-level metadata. Autoscaler events must be emitted to metrics topic 'dedicated.autoscaler.events' with fields: timestamp, account_id, event_type, delta_gpus, reason. Hooks: console must show pending autoscale events and estimated time-to-serve for queued requests. Integration: ENG-44121 to add metric emission and ENG-44200 for admission control enforcement.
measurement_queries_examples: Grafana queries (pseudo): 1) per_minute_served = sum(rate(tokens_served_total{account_id=\"$account\"}[1m])) by (account_id) 2) per_minute_median_5m = histogram_quantile(0.5, increase(per_minute_served[5m])) 3) shortfall_minutes = sum_over_time((per_minute_served < 0.9 * CTPM) [30d:1m]) 4) error_budget_fraction = shortfall_minutes / (30 * 24 * 60)
legal_and_sales_notes: Requested by Sales: simpler banding preferred for contract negotiation. Legal prefers precise definitions for measurement and exclusions. Finance requested that credits be applied to committed monthly fee first, then offset future invoices rather than refunds. Proposed compromise: use SmoothCredit v1 for calculation but publish an illustrative 'credit table' for sales to include in early negotiations. Legal review link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Legal/pages/throughput-sla-drafts. Sales FAQ draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xq-sla-faq
open_questions: Should measurement use 1m or 5m aggregation for primary signal? (Pros: 1m detects short spikes; 5m reduces noise)
Do we include KV cache hit-rate adjustments to effective throughput when computing shortfall?
Acceptance of time-decay weights in SmoothCredit v1 (product prefers flat window for transparency; SRE prefers recent-incident weighting)
What external audit log do we expose to customers for dispute resolution? (raw metric dump vs signed snapshots)
